chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Things come to us that we neither recognize in the Book of God nor in the Sunnah; so shall we apply our reasoning in them?'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Know that if you are correct, you will not be rewarded, and if you err, you would have lied against God, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.سُنَّةٍ: Sunnah — Prophetic tradition, second primary source of law
key_terms.كَذَبْتَ عَلَى اللَّهِ: lying against God — falsely attributing religious rulings to God without divine sanction
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: Book of God — the Quran, primary source of Islamic law
key_terms.لَمْ تُؤْجَرْ: not rewarded — even correctness via personal opinion carries no divine recompense

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about applying personal opinion (ra'y) in matters not found in the Quran or Sunnah?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether personal opinion (ra'y) may be applied to matters not addressed in the Quran or Sunnah. The Imam categorically prohibits this: even a correct answer reached by personal reasoning yields no divine reward, while an incorrect one constitutes lying against God — a double condemnation that forecloses any juristic justification for the practice. This hadith is a cornerstone proof-text in Shia jurisprudence for the impermissibility of qiyas (analogical reasoning) and ra'y (personal opinion) as independent sources of religious law.
word_analysis: so shall we apply our reasoning

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Musna Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Things (certain matters) are referred to us, neither do we recognise these in the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> not Sunnah. So can we apply our opinion in these?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but if you are correct, you will not be Rewarded (for being correct), and if you err, you would have lied against Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Muthanna al-Hannat from abu Basir who has said the following. “I asked (Imam) abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) saying, ‘We face such issue about which there is nothing said in the book of Allah or in the Sunnah, tradition of the holy Prophet (s.a.). Can use our own opinion in such matters?’”
The Imam replied, “No, you must not do so. If you would find the truth you will receive no rewards for it an if missed the truth you have forged lies against Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious.”
